subject: science
title: Seasons
about: The four seasons in order, what each looks like in North Carolina (fall leaves, cold winters with some snow, spring rain and flowers, hot summers), longer summer days and shorter winter days, and what people and animals do. Seasons are not named in NC's 2023 Grade 1 science standards; this is a bridge topic filed under ESS.1.1.1 (sun patterns), the closest objective.
tip: Each month, ask him what season it is and for one clue from outside the window that proves it.

cards.q: How many seasons are there in a year?
cards.note: Fall, winter, spring, summer, then fall again.
Fall leaves drop, then the cold of winter comes.
After the cold, things warm up and flowers come back.
Spring warms up into hot summer. School lets out.

cards.q: After summer comes fall again. What do the seasons do every year?
cards.note: The seasons go around in the same order every year. That is a pattern.

cards.q: In fall, many North Carolina leaves turn red, orange and yellow. Then what do they do?
cards.note: That is why we call this season fall.

cards.q: Which season is the coldest in North Carolina?
cards.note: Winter is December, January and February here.

cards.q: In North Carolina, when might you see snow?
cards.note: Some winters bring snow and some do not. The mountains get the most.

cards.q: In spring the days get warmer and it rains. What do plants start to do?
cards.note: Spring brings flowers, buds and new green leaves.

cards.q: Which season is the hottest in North Carolina?
cards.note: Summer here is hot and sticky. Many families cool off at a pool or the beach.

cards.q: In which season does the sun stay up the longest?
cards.note: In summer it is still light after supper. That is one of the sun's patterns.

cards.q: In winter, when does it get dark outside?
cards.note: Winter days are short. Summer days are long.

cards.q: What do you wear outside on a cold winter day?
cards.note: People change what they wear as the seasons change.

cards.q: In fall, what do many people rake up in their yards?
cards.note: Jumping in the leaf pile is the best part.

cards.q: Some birds fly to warmer places for the winter. When do they come back?
cards.note: Hummingbirds leave North Carolina in fall and come back in spring.

cards.q: A black bear rests through much of the cold winter. Where does it rest?
cards.note: North Carolina has black bears. In the cold mountains they rest in dens through winter.
